newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India has bought one kerosene cargo for November.
newsitem.headline: India has bought one kerosene cargo for November.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has bought one 45,000-tonne cargo of superior kerosene in its tender for November delivery, traders said early Monday.
The cargo was purchased from US major Mobil at $2.08 a barrel on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Madras or Haldia on the Indian east coast for delivery during November 1-10, traders said.
Traders had expected India to buy about three cargoes and said that they were surprised that India did not buy from other more aggressive offers made to the tender.
They said other east coast offers were made around $1.92-$1.94 per barrel premiums to MidEast quotes, c-and-f basis.
West coast offers were seen around $1.39-$1.49 per barrel premiums to MidEast quotes, c-and-f.
Traders making these aggressive offers said they have not yet received telexes from IOC to confirm whether or not they have been awarded.
In its previous tender for October delivery, IOC bought five cargoes of kerosene totalling 210,000 tonnes.
The awarded levels in that tender were at a premium of $2.25-$2.30 per barrel to MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f east coast. A free-on-board price was also awarded in that tender at 65 cents per barrel.
